title: Fix a child's wrong answer on a block sum
instruction: the child's sum is wrong: fix the blocks on the answer mat, putting any spare block in the spare tray
context: Helping children learn means checking their work and correcting it, not redoing everything. A printed card reads 2 + 3 = and the child laid out six blocks; the fix is to take exactly one away.
setup: Positions are measured on the table from the midpoint between the two arm bases: forward is away from the arms, left and right as seen from behind the arms. (1) Card: a white card, fixed flat, centred 43 cm forward and 5 cm right, printed in black block characters 2.5 cm wide and 3.5 cm tall reading "2 + 3 =". (2) Answer mat: a yellow sheet, 26 cm front to back by 24 cm left to right and 0.8 mm thick, fixed flat, centred 21 cm forward and 20 cm right. (3) Spare tray: four grey walls, 1 cm thick and 3 cm tall, fixed around a 10 x 10 cm space, centred 15 cm forward and 6 cm left. (4) Six orange wooden blocks, 5 cm cubes of 50 g each, loose, standing on the answer mat in two rows of three: at 12, 21 and 30 cm forward, in rows 14 and 26 cm right. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Scored once, after the episode ends. A block is on the answer mat when it rests still with its centre over the mat and its underside within 1 cm of the table, and in the spare tray when it rests still with its centre inside the tray's walls. 1.0: exactly five blocks on the mat and the sixth in the spare tray. 0.5: exactly five on the mat, the sixth elsewhere. 0.0: any other number on the mat, including the untouched six.
reset_notes: Put all six blocks back on the answer mat in their two rows of three. The card, mat and tray are fixed (tape) and stay in place.
fidelity: Dream Labs' YAM station replica in Isaac Lab-Arena (Isaac Sim). The blocks are rigid 5 cm cubes with default friction. The card's characters are thin black boxes on a white board, and the mat is a thin fixed sheet. There is no child in the scene.
